cards.text: The writer of this letter has just talked about the Spirit God has given (1 John 3:24). Now he calls his readers beloved and warns them: do not believe every spirit. Friend, that's the rule for every text that says you won a FREE cruise.

cards.question: The writer tells his beloved readers not to believe every spirit. What should they do instead?

answers.text: Test them to see if they're from God
Stay far away from every spirit
Trust the one that sounds the kindest

cards.question: The writer gives his readers a reason to test the spirits: many false ___ have gone out into the world.

cards.text: I test every batch with one bite, okay FOUR bites, but the writer's test for a spirit is simpler. It all comes down to what a spirit says about Jesus.

cards.question: The writer gives a test for the Spirit of God. What does every spirit from God confess about Jesus Christ?

answers.text: He has come in the flesh
He is an angel from heaven

cards.question: The writer says a spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God.

cards.text: The writer even names the spirit that doesn't confess Jesus. It's the spirit of the antichrist, and his readers had already heard it was coming.

cards.question: The writer's readers had heard the spirit of the antichrist was coming. When does he say it shows up in the world?

answers.text: It came and went long ago

cards.text: Friend, that news would send me diving back under the takeout menus in my old junk drawer. But the writer turns to his readers with good news.

cards.question: The writer calls his readers little children and tells them they're from God and have overcome. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Someone greater is in them than in the world
They far outnumber the false prophets in the world
They were taught better than the false prophets

cards.text: Then the writer turns back to the ones his readers have overcome. They are of the world, so they speak from the world's perspective.

cards.question: The writer says the world won't listen to the ones who speak from the world's perspective.

cards.text: Now the writer flips it around and says, "We are from God." Some people listen to his side, and some tune it out like I tune out my oven timer, right up until I smell smoke.

cards.question: The writer says whoever knows God listens to his side.

cards.text: And whoever is not from God doesn't listen to the writer's side. Then he wraps it up: "That is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception."
